Proposition
[Classical solutions are viscosity solutions] ↗ def:viscosity-solution-cauchy-problem 1. ch10:10.1-prop-1\group Viscosity Solutions

If $u \in C^1(\R ^n \times [0,\infty ))$ solves (1) and if $u$ is bounded and uniformly continuous, then $u$ is a viscosity solution. That is, any classical solution of $u_t + H(Du,x) = 0$ is also a viscosity solution.

Proof

\sketch At a local maximum or minimum of $u-v$, differentiability gives $Du=Dv$ and $u_t=v_t$. Substitution into the classical Hamilton–Jacobi equation gives equality, hence both viscosity inequalities.

□
